text:
mari: Quick question — looking at the latest perf profiles for fused attention on A100. Any low-hanging epilogue fusions we should try? I’m seeing ~12% tail spend in post-attn softmax+proj.

liam: Which profile/config? can you paste numbers?

mari: perf snippet (seq=128, bsz=8):
```
- flash_v1 (no fusion): 12.4 ms
- fused_qkv_pack: 9.1 ms
- fused_qkv_pack + bias+rope: 8.7 ms
- fused_epilogue_try1 (inline softmax+proj): 8.2 ms
note: CPU-side memcpy ~0.5ms for epilogue buffers
```

sophia: :thinking: epilogue_try1 looks promising. what's the memory bw usage for that kernel?

ryan: nvprof shows the epilogue kernel doing loads/stores ~32 GB/s; toggles we tried: `KVCACHE_PAGE=1`, `PREFETCH_EPILOGUE=1`, `EPILOGUE_VECTORIZE=1`.

perf-bot: Perf alert: commit abc123 increased p99 on long sequences by ~4% while improving median (epilogue vectorize). See nightly perf run.

liam: Idea — instead of separate epilogue pass for bias+rope then softmax+proj, try applying bias+rope during QKV packing so the later softmax+proj can operate on already-rope'd, bias-corrected tensors. That should reduce memory traffic.

mari: Agree. Also consider keeping softmax+proj in-register (no external temp) if we can reduce register pressure. I can sketch a kernel that does: pack -> apply rope/bias -> compute attention -> inline softmax -> output proj.

sophia: If you prototype, remember paged KV cache (paged attention) breaks assumptions about contiguous KV. We need a fallback path for paged layouts.

ryan: For paged KV we probably need two modes: 1) in-place fusion when KV pages are contiguous; 2) streamed epilogue that consumes small temp buffers per page. Heuristic selects based on `kv_pages` and `seq_tail`.

mari: Heuristic proposal: `if kv_pages == 1 && seq_tail < 64 && batch_tokens > 2048 => use epilogue_fused_fastpath else use safe_streamed_path`. Thoughts?

liam: Also run microbenchmarks across seq_len distributions, not just fixed seq. Fusion helps short sequences a lot and can regress on long sequences (register pressure / spills).

mari: Will prototype and add bench results to repo/bench. I’ll aim for a small kernel patch this week. cc @eng-tools for perf infra. :rocket:

eng-tools: Got it — tag the PR with `perf/attn-fusion-scan` and include `bench.json` output. Perf bot will pick it up on the nightly matrix.

ryan: One more caution — fusing softmax+proj can change FP16 reduction order; add fp32 reference runs and a small numerical unit test to catch regressions.

mari: Yep — will add fp32 baseline and a deterministic unit test on a couple of edge-case inputs. Will post results here when I have the draft.

liam: Thanks — if you want I can help with the register allocation sketch and a quick autotune sweep for block sizes.

mari: Appreciate it, thanks!
